originalTitle: Why Uganda seems to be winning the battle against Ebola as virus spreads in DR Congo
summary: Uganda discharged its last Ebola patient from hospital roughly two weeks ago.
content:
Uganda said previous outbreaks have taught the authorities how to respond efficiently to Ebola

The Ebola outbreak in the east of the Democratic Republic of Congo has become the second-worst on record, with the official death toll passing a grim milestone of 1,500.

Experts believe the true number of fatalities during this outbreak, which was declared in May, is much higher. And in another alarming update, authorities in DR Congo confirmed on Thursday that the virus was spreading much faster than in previous outbreaks.

Next door in Uganda, a country that also reported infections in May, the picture is entirely different.

The country's health minister described a "moment of joy" as the last Ebola patient was released from hospital two weeks ago.

Uganda only ever recorded 20 cases and two deaths from the virus.

According to Dr Kasonde Mwinga, the World Health Organization's Uganda chief, the relatively low number of casualties was not "by luck or chance".

"It's because people invested in preparedness," she told the BBC.

This outbreak is the 17th to have emerged in DR Congo since Ebola was discovered 50 years ago. By comparison Uganda has had nine since 2000, with officials there saying lessons learnt from past tragedies have allowed them to stop the disease ripping through the country on various occasions.

One example is the case of a 12-year-old girl who arrived at a hospital in the central district of Luwero in 2011.

Her symptoms sparked caution: she was isolated, medics wore personal protective equipment when treating her and when she died three hours later her body was carefully sealed in a coffin. These precautions were able to halt the spread of what a blood sample later confirmed to be Ebola.

"We know Ebola. It's been here a few times, we know how to deal with it," government spokesperson Alan Kasujja told the BBC's Newsday programme.

Uganda's first known case this time was a man from DR Congo who crossed the border for treatment.

Once health authorities confirmed multiple cases had been imported from DR Congo, they activated a specialist Ebola treatment centre at Mulago hospital, in the capital city, Kampala.

The facility, which was used during an outbreak of Ebola last year, held leftover medical supplies and had an "emergency medical team" on standby, Dr David Kaggwa, head of the facility, said.

"It was a matter of sorting and ordering a few more supplies, and then actually in one day we were ready to receive the patients. So, it is easy, it's not that we're starting from scratch," he said.

What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

'They said it isn't real': Ebola rumours fuel attacks on health workers

Out of the 20 people who tested positive in Uganda, 15 came from DR Congo.

The first two cases, it is thought, might not have known what condition they had. But after Uganda and DR Congo jointly declared the Ebola outbreak on 15 May, people with symptoms - which include headaches, fever and vomiting - "came direct to the treatment unit," Dr Kaggwa said.

He suspects that because these patients did not pass through general hospitals, and come into contact with those patients and medics, there was little opportunity for community transmission.

In a bid to stop the disease spreading, the authorities also closed the border between Uganda and DR Congo, despite the financial impact this would have on Ugandans who travel between the two countries to trade.

Uganda acted fast, but it also had an advantage over DR Congo when it came to responding to the virus.

Before the first cases were reported in DR Congo, Ebola had been spreading undetected for weeks. This was because health officials poised to pick up outbreaks had been testing for common species of Ebola, and not the rare species behind the current outbreak, named Bundibugyo.

Uganda only detected its first case after DR Congo had identified and publicised multiple infections - knowledge of the outbreak was out in the open and Uganda could therefore act quickly to contain the virus.

At-risk communities in Uganda have complied with prevention efforts, a government spokesperson says

"Surveillance mechanisms were put in place then it was easy to identify all the patients quickly," Dr Kaggwa said.

Comparatively, DR Congo has had a harder time with surveillance and contact tracing.

One field investigator tasked with tracking the virus across Bunia, a city at the epicentre of the outbreak, told Reuters that surveillance had been hampered by poor planning, logistical bottlenecks and the recruitment of inexperienced staff.

"We discover the disease only after it has already spread," Dr Moubarack Kano said. "We're just chasing it."

This is not helped by the insecurity that plagues eastern DR Congo. Ituri, the province at the centre of the outbreak, has been under military rule for several years as the army tries to crack down on dozens of armed groups there.

Further south of Ituri there are large areas held by the M23 rebels, a powerful militia that says it has managed to contain the outbreak.

Its Ebola response co-ordinator Dr Fred Kaniki attributed the achievement to early detection and contact tracing, telling the BBC: "In the course of a month we registered two more cases originating from those index cases and successfully followed up 400 people."

But the M23 conflict and other pockets of violence have displaced millions of people in the region - and that makes surveillance difficult in DR Congo. Artisanal mining and cross-border trade also means Ebola has more chances to spread as people are constantly on the move.

In contrast, Uganda managed to quarantine more than 6,000 contacts of people known to have Ebola during the outbreak. These contacts were isolated for an incubation period of 21 days.

"That is very, very important because usually cases come from those contacts," said Dr Kaggwa.

chineseTitle: 当病毒在刚果民主共和国传播时，为什么乌干达似乎正在赢得抗击埃博拉的战斗
chineseSummary: 乌干达最后一名埃博拉患者大约两周前出院。
chineseContent:
乌干达表示，之前的疫情爆发教会了当局如何有效应对埃博拉病毒

刚果民主共和国东部的埃博拉疫情已成为有记录以来第二严重的埃博拉疫情，官方公布的死亡人数已突破 1,500 人这一严峻的里程碑。

专家认为，五月份宣布的这次疫情爆发的真实死亡人数要高得多。另一项令人震惊的最新消息是，刚果民主共和国当局周四证实，该病毒的传播速度比之前的疫情要快得多。

隔壁的乌干达也于五月份报告了感染病例，情况则完全不同。

该国卫生部长描述了两周前最后一名埃博拉患者出院时的“欢乐时刻”。

乌干达仅记录了 20 例病例和 2 例死亡病例。

世界卫生组织乌干达负责人卡松德·姆温加博士表示，相对较低的伤亡人数并非“幸运或偶然”。

“这是因为人们投入了准备工作，”她告诉英国广播公司。

这是自 50 年前发现埃博拉病毒以来，刚果民主共和国爆发的第 17 次疫情。相比之下，自 2000 年以来乌干达已有 9 例病例，该国官员表示，从过去的悲剧中吸取的教训使他们能够阻止这种疾病在该国多次肆虐。

一名 12 岁女孩的案例就是一个例子，她于 2011 年来到卢韦罗中心区的一家医院。

她的症状引发了人们的警惕：她被隔离，医护人员在治疗她时穿着个人防护装备，三小时后她去世时，她的尸体被小心地密封在棺材里。这些预防措施能够阻止后来被血液样本证实为埃博拉病毒的传播。

“我们了解埃博拉病毒。它已经出现过几次了，我们知道如何应对，”政府发言人艾伦·卡苏贾 (Alan Kasujja) 告诉英国广播公司的《新闻日报》节目。

乌干达此次已知的首例病例是一名来自刚果民主共和国的男子，他越过边境接受治疗。

卫生当局确认有多例从刚果民主共和国输入的病例后，他们启动了首都坎帕拉穆拉戈医院的埃博拉专家治疗中心。

该设施负责人戴维·卡格瓦（David Kaggwa）博士说，该设施去年埃博拉疫情爆发期间使用过，里面存放着剩余的医疗用品，并有一支“紧急医疗队”待命。

“这只是分类和订购更多物资的问题，然后实际上在一天之内我们就准备好接收患者了。所以，这很容易，而不是我们从头开始，”他说。

什么是埃博拉病毒？为什么阻止最新的疫情如此困难？

“他们说这不是真的”：埃博拉谣言加剧了对卫生工作者的袭击

在乌干达检测呈阳性的 20 人中，有 15 人来自刚果民主共和国。

据认为，前两个病例可能不知道自己患有什么病症。但卡格瓦博士说，乌干达和刚果民主共和国于 5 月 15 日联合宣布埃博拉疫情爆发后，出现头痛、发烧和呕吐等症状的人“直接来到治疗室”。

他怀疑，由于这些患者没有经过综合医院，没有与那些患者和医护人员接触，因此社区传播的机会很少。

为了阻止疾病传播，当局还关闭了乌干达和刚果民主共和国之间的边境，尽管这会对在两国之间进行贸易的乌干达人造成经济影响。

乌干达行动迅速，但在应对病毒方面也比刚果民主共和国更具优势。

在刚果民主共和国报告第一例病例之前，埃博拉病毒已在未被发现的情况下传播了数周。这是因为准备应对疫情的卫生官员一直在检测埃博拉病毒的常见物种，而不是当前疫情爆发的稀有物种 Bundibugyo。

在刚果民主共和国发现并公布多起感染病例后，乌干达才发现第一例病例——疫情爆发的信息已公开，因此乌干达可以迅速采取行动遏制该病毒。

政府发言人表示，乌干达的高危社区已遵守预防措施

卡格瓦博士说：“监测机制到位后，就可以很容易地快速识别所有患者。”

相比之下，刚果民主共和国在监测和接触者追踪方面遇到了困难。

一名负责在疫情中心城市布尼亚追踪病毒的现场调查员告诉路透社，由于规划不善、后勤瓶颈和招募缺乏经验的工作人员，监测工作受到阻碍。

穆巴拉克·卡诺博士说：“我们只有在这种疾病已经传播后才发现它。” “我们只是在追寻它。”

刚果民主共和国东部的不安全局势无助于解决这一问题。处于疫情中心的伊图里省多年来一直处于军事统治之下，军队试图镇压那里的数十个武装团体。

在伊图里以南，有大片地区被“M23”叛军控制，这是一支强大的民兵组织，声称已成功控制了疫情的爆发。

其埃博拉应对协调员 Fred Kaniki 博士将这一成就归功于早期发现和接触者追踪，他告诉 BBC：“在一个月内，我们又登记了两例源自这些指示病例的病例，并成功跟踪了 400 人。”

但 M23 冲突和其他暴力事件已导致该地区数百万人流离失所，这使得刚果民主共和国的监控变得困难。手工采矿和跨境贸易也意味着，随着人们不断流动，埃博拉病毒有更多的传播机会。

相比之下，乌干达在疫情爆发期间成功隔离了 6000 多名已知感染埃博拉病毒的接触者。这些接触者被隔离潜伏期为 21 天。

卡格瓦博士说：“这非常非常重要，因为病例通常来自这些接触者。”

卡苏贾表示同意。 “我想说，我们的成功主要归功于我们的及时性和完整性
